basics.name: Knock-down and flat-pack furniture connectors (cam-lock / Häfele Minifix, Lamello Clamex and Tenso P-System, Häfele and Blum catalogues, IKEA wedge dowel)
basics.url: Lamello P-System (Clamex P, Tenso P, Divario, Bisco, LC P-16): https://lamello.com/products/p-system ; Lamello System (4 mm biscuit groove, Clamex S, E20): https://lamello.com/products/lamello-system ; Lamello Drilling System (Cabineo, Invis Mx2): https://lamello.com/products/drilling-system ; example product page: https://lamello.com/products/p-system/clamex-p-14 ; Häfele America 'Connectors and Shelf Supports' catalogue chapter 11 (January 2015, 189 pages, hosted by a reseller): https://p11.secure.hostingprod.com/@site.homedecorhardware.com/ssl/hafele-catalog-2017/11-Connectors-and-Shelf-Supports.pdf ; Blum motion technologies: https://www.blum.com/us/en/products/motion-technologies/4-motiontechnologies/ and CLIP top hinge: https://www.blum.com/us/en/products/hingesystems/clip-top/programme/ ; IKEA Museum wedge dowel story: https://ikeamuseum.com/en/explore/the-story-of-ikea/the-wedge-dowel/ ; IKEA FACTS wedge dowel sheet (2015): https://preview.thenewsmarket.com/Previews/IKEA/DocumentAssets/436946.pdf ; wedge dowel patent US9447804B2: https://patents.google.com/patent/US9447804B2/en ; background: Wikipedia 'Furniture screw' (knock-down fastener section): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furniture_screw and DT Online 'Knock Down Fittings, Brackets and Plates': https://wiki.dtonline.org/index.php/Knock_Down_Fittings,_Brackets_and_Plates . Häfele's own websites (hafele.com, hafele.co.uk, hafele.com.au, hafele.de) returned HTTP 403 to every automated request, so no live Häfele page was opened
basics.resource_type: Supplier catalogue (manufacturers' online catalogues and a PDF catalogue chapter), plus a manufacturer's museum page, fact sheet and patent for the IKEA wedge dowel
basics.cost: Free to read (catalogues, product pages, CAD downloads and the patent are free). The connectors themselves are paid; Lamello P-System connectors also need a special cutter (Zeta P2 biscuit joiner or a CNC machine), which is an expensive professional tool [uncertain: price not checked]
basics.license: All rights reserved for all of them: 'Copyright 2015 Häfele America Co. All rights reserved' in the catalogue PDF; '© Inter IKEA Systems B.V. 2026' on the IKEA Museum page and '© Inter IKEA Systems B.V. 2015' on the fact sheet; Lamello and Blum pages are commercial pages (no open licence seen) [uncertain for Lamello and Blum exact wording]. Link to them, do not copy text or drawings. The patent text (US9447804B2) is a US government publication and can be quoted freely, though its drawings are best redrawn. DT Online wiki is CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial), and Wikipedia is CC BY-SA
basics.language: English used here. Lamello's site offers about 15 languages (German, French, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Spanish, Swedish and others); Blum runs country sites in about 40 languages; Häfele publishes country catalogues in many languages [uncertain: Häfele language list not checked because its sites were blocked]; IKEA Museum is English and Swedish [uncertain]
basics.year: Lamello founded its wooden biscuit in 1955 (Lamello page); P-System and Clamex P from about 2010 [uncertain], pages current in 2026. Häfele Minifix developed in 1983 (per a secondary buying guide in search results) [uncertain]; the Häfele America catalogue chapter opened is dated January 2015 (file path says 2017). Blum founded 1952, first hinge 1964, 'four motion technologies' from 2015 (Blum history page). IKEA wedge dowel: patent priority 13 January 2012, granted 20 September 2016; first machine-made wedge dowel product on sale in 2013 (TROMVIK); LISABO table won a Red Dot award in 2016
basics.access_barrier: None for people in a normal browser (Lamello, Blum, IKEA, Google Patents all open freely). For automated tools, Häfele blocks everything (HTTP 403 on all Häfele domains and on some resellers), and Lamello needs cookies to stop a redirect loop. Some Häfele catalogue chapters survive as PDFs on reseller hosting
basics.image_license: All rights reserved (manufacturer photos, renders, technical drawings, CAD files and videos). Lamello CAD downloads (DWG, DXF, STEP) are offered for designing with its connectors, not for republishing [uncertain]. Patent drawings are public-domain US government records. Wikipedia's knock-down fastener images come from Wikimedia Commons with their own open licences
basics.authority_level: Manufacturer (Häfele, Lamello, Blum, IKEA/Inter IKEA Systems). Very reliable for how their own connectors work and their numbers; not neutral (brand names instead of generic names, e.g. Minifix for cam connector, Clamex for lever-cam biscuit connector, TIP-ON for push-to-open)

coverage.covers: Panel and furniture joints that can be taken apart or put together without glue or tools. Häfele catalogue chapter 11 (189 pages) covers lightweight-panel connectors, RTA (ready-to-assemble) connectors (Rafix 20 system, Minifix system, Maxifix system, Tab 18, Tab V, Rasant Tab, Quick Dowel, DC-25 dowel/cam connector, Confa 35, Solo 32), special connectors (Giro-bolt lock, surface connectors, Keku push-in and suspension fittings, Keku AD double partition fastener, Uni-Connector, modular connection fittings), joint and worktop connectors (Zipbolt, Maxifix worktop connector, Flipbolt), standards and brackets, shelf supports and shelf hold-downs, catches (magnetic, push-to-open 'touch' latches, ball, roller, spring catches), connecting brackets, bed fittings (Berliner fitting, bail-clip connecting fitting), keyhole plates, cross dowels and screws. Lamello covers about 20 connector types in three systems: P-System (Clamex P detachable lever connector in several variants, Tenso P self-clamping glue connector, Divario P-18 slide-in connector, Bisco P aligning element, LC P-16 lightweight-panel insert), Lamello System on a 4 mm groove (original wood biscuit, C10/C20 clear plastic biscuits, E20 self-clamping hammer-in element, Clamex S-20 and S-18 detachable connectors) and a drilling system (Cabineo one-piece cabinet connector, Cabineo X, Invis Mx2 magnet-driven hidden connector). Blum covers moving cabinet hardware rather than joints: tool-free clip-on concealed hinges (CLIP top), four 'motion technologies' (BLUMOTION soft close, TIP-ON push-to-open, TIP-ON BLUMOTION, SERVO-DRIVE electric opening), lift systems (AVENTOS) and drawer runners. IKEA covers one clever type in depth: the wedge dowel (a grooved dowel that clicks into a hole and pulls parts tight)
coverage.organisation: Häfele: by product family and brand name, grouped by use (lightweight panel connectors, RTA connectors, special connectors, joint and work-surface connectors, shelf supports, catches, brackets, bed fittings, furniture connectors, screws), with technical 'Information' pages that explain the principle (e.g. the Minifix clock-face tightening diagram) before the ordering tables. Hard for beginners because the names are brand names (Minifix, Rafix, Maxifix, Keku, Zipbolt). Lamello: by 'system' (which groove or hole you cut) and then by function (detachable, self-clamping for gluing, slide-in, aligning), which works well because it starts from what you can make with your tool. Lamello also has an online 'product finder' and a 'P-System configurator' that picks the connector from the joint angle. Blum: by product family (lift, hinge, box, runner, pocket, organisation systems, motion technologies) and, for motion technologies, by 'type of motion' (mechanical soft close; electrical opening and soft close; mechanical opening and soft close; mechanical opening)
coverage.scope_match: medium: the product ranges themselves are standard furniture hardware (out of scope), but they contain several clever connector TYPES that fit the encyclopedia well: cam-and-bolt connectors, lever-cam biscuit connectors, self-clamping spring connectors, slide-in clamping connectors, hand-pushed expanding bolts, hidden hanging fittings, push-to-open latches, clip-on hinges, the magnet-driven hidden connector and the IKEA wedge dowel. Woodworking/CNC joinery is in scope but lowest priority
coverage.taxonomy_used: Commercial, by product family and brand, with a function split inside. Häfele chapter 11 has 12 top-level groups in its contents: Lightweight Panel Connectors; RTA Connectors; Special Connectors; Joint and Work Surface Connectors; Standards and Brackets; Shelf Supports; Catches; Connecting Brackets; Bed Fittings; Furniture Connectors; Screws; UV Glass Bonding. Lamello uses 3 systems (P-System form-locking groove; Lamello System 4 mm groove; Drilling System) and within them 4 functions: detachable (Clamex, Divario, Cabineo, Invis), self-clamping glue aid (Tenso, E20), aligning (Bisco, biscuits) and anchoring in lightweight panels (LC P-16). Blum classes motion by 'type of motion' in 4 motion technologies. Wikipedia and DT Online use the generic class 'knock-down (KD) fittings' (fasteners designed for repeated assembly and disassembly), with DT Online listing 9 kinds (connecting/modesty blocks, connector nuts and bolts, cross dowels/barrel nuts, cam-lock fitting, Confirmat screws, cabinet connector screws, cover caps, shelf supports, worktop connector bolts)
coverage.example_types: cam-lock connector (cam and bolt, eccentric connector; Häfele Minifix, Rafix, Maxifix); cam connector with expanding bolt pushed in by hand (spreading bolt); one-piece cam connector for CNC face drilling (Lamello Cabineo); lever-cam groove connector, detachable (Lamello Clamex P, Clamex S); self-clamping spring glue connector (Lamello Tenso P); self-clamping hammer-in biscuit (Lamello E20); slide-in self-clamping shelf connector (Lamello Divario); magnet-driven hidden connector turned by a magnet through the panel (Lamello Invis Mx2); wooden biscuit (plate joint) and clear plastic biscuit; IKEA wedge dowel (grooved click-in dowel that pulls parts together); one-time push-in snap dowel (Häfele Quick Dowel, 'non-releasable'); cross dowel and barrel nut with connecting bolt; Confirmat screw (one-piece furniture connector screw); push-in panel fitting (Keku) and hanging/suspension panel fitting that releases without tools (Keku suspension fitting); bail-clip bed/connecting fitting (press together, snap the bail over); Berliner bed fitting (hook-in plate); keyhole plate (hang on a screw head); Giro-bolt lock (turn-bolt locking connector released with a hex key); worktop connector (Zipbolt, Maxifix worktop, dog-bone bolt); clip-on concealed hinge (Blum CLIP top, doors 'snap on and off' without tools); push-to-open latch (Blum TIP-ON, Häfele push and touch latches); soft-close damper (Blum BLUMOTION); adhesive-cartridge insert for honeycomb panels (Häfele Aerofix 100)
coverage.making_methods: Woodworking and cabinet making in sheet materials (particleboard, MDF, plywood, lightweight honeycomb panels, solid wood), CNC routing and drilling (Lamello P-System and Cabineo designed for CNC), hand power tools (biscuit joiner, drill jigs), and mass-produced flat-pack furniture. Not aimed at 3D printing, though the principles (cam, wedge dowel, spring clamp, keyhole) can be printed [uncertain: printability is an inference, not stated by the sources]
coverage.item_count: Häfele: chapter 11 of the Häfele America catalogue is 189 pages with about 70 named product families in its contents; Häfele's web shop says 'over 250 furniture connectors' (seen only in a search snippet) [uncertain]. Lamello: about 20 connector types in 3 systems (counted from its pages). Blum: 4 motion technologies plus about 10 hinge application groups for CLIP top. IKEA: 1 type (wedge dowel) in several versions
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: hand-release only / detachable: yes (Clamex P 'open the connection time and time again with the rotating lever'; Keku suspension fitting 'releases without tools'; Invis Mx2 released by reversing the drill; Minifix spreading bolt 'can be unscrewed again by hand'). self-locking: yes (cam connectors that pull tight and resist loosening; Maxifix has a 'locking device on the outside of the cam' to prevent loosening; the wedge dowel locks by friction in a tapering groove). one-way / permanent: yes (Häfele Quick Dowel is a 'fast, one time, non-releasable connector'; Tenso is meant to be glued). indexing/detent: little (shelf supports with locking, catches). over-centre: partly (the Minifix cam has a closing, tightening and re-tightening zone up to a 195 degree stop; bail-clip bed fittings snap over) [uncertain whether the sources call this over-centre]. compliant: yes in practice (Tenso's tension springs; E20's curved ridges; plastic spreading dowels) though not named as compliant. print-in-place: no. gear trains: no. powered connectors: partly (Blum SERVO-DRIVE electric opening; Lamello Invis Mx2 is driven by a rotating magnet on a cordless drill, not powered in place). torque-limiting: no. adhesive types: little (Häfele Aerofix 100 holds a one-component PUR adhesive in a cartridge, fully cured in 16 hours; Lamello Tenso and E20 are clamping aids for wood glue; Häfele lists 'UV glass bonding')
coverage.entry_structure: Häfele PDF: family name, bullet list of features, material and finish, item numbers, dimensioned line drawings, drilling data, and for key families an 'Information' page on how it works (e.g. Minifix: 0-75 degrees closing distance 3 mm, 75-165 degrees tightening 2 mm, 165-195 degrees re-tightening 0.5 mm). Lamello product page: short description, features, applications, technical specification table (tolerances, minimum thickness, tensile and shear strength in particle board, MDF and beech), CAD downloads, operation manual, videos. Blum: overview, product range by application, assembly and download tabs. IKEA: story page and fact sheet; the patent gives claims and drawings
coverage.audience_level: professional (cabinet makers, furniture manufacturers, CNC shops, kitchen fitters); usable by skilled hobbyists. The IKEA pages are written for the general public

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: Lamello's pages are clear and function-led (detachable, self-clamping, invisible) with videos and times per step; the Häfele Minifix clock-face explanation is excellent. But everything is buried under brand names (Minifix, Rafix, Keku, Clamex, TIP-ON) with no generic glossary, and catalogues assume you know what a 32 mm system or an RTA connector is
usefulness.has_images: yes: Häfele has dimensioned line drawings and photos for every family; Lamello has renders, photos and CAD; Blum has photos and application images; the patent has technical drawings; Wikipedia has a Commons gallery of cam lock, barrel nut, T-nut, insert nut and hanger bolt
usefulness.has_animations: yes, video: Lamello has product and tutorial videos for each connector (e.g. 'Clamex P-14 - Detachable furniture connector', 'Divario P-18 - Self-clamping, invisible connector for slide insertion'); Blum has application videos and customer interviews; Häfele videos exist on its (blocked) sites [uncertain]. No interactive 3D models seen
usefulness.gaps: No neutral, generic classification across makers (each uses its own brand names); no comparison of cam-lock vs lever connector vs wedge dowel vs knock-down bolt by strength, reusability or tool needed; almost nothing on making these joints yourself without the special cutter, jig or CNC; nothing about 3D-printed or laser-cut versions; Häfele's current web catalogue could not be opened (only a 2015 PDF chapter); Blum is about motion hardware (hinges, runners, lifts), not panel joints; the IKEA wedge dowel is explained only at press-release level (the patent is the only detailed source)
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: Yes for Lamello and Blum: stable readable URLs per product (e.g. https://lamello.com/products/p-system/clamex-p-14, https://www.blum.com/us/en/products/motion-technologies/tip-on/overview/). Google Patents gives a stable page for the wedge dowel (https://patents.google.com/patent/US9447804B2/en) and IKEA Museum a stable story page. Häfele product URLs follow the pattern /product/<name>/P-<number>/ but could not be opened here and block bots [uncertain]
usefulness.reusable_data: Not reusable as data: all catalogues are all rights reserved and there is no API or open dataset. The type names (cam connector, wedge dowel, knock-down fitting) can be used freely as vocabulary. Wikipedia's knock-down fastener text is CC BY-SA and DT Online's list is CC BY-NC-SA (non-commercial only). Patent text can be quoted
usefulness.maintained: Yes: Lamello, Blum and IKEA Museum pages are live and current (IKEA page © 2026; Blum pages list 2026 markets; Lamello shows 2026 customer reports [uncertain on exact dates]). The Häfele PDF opened is a 2015 edition on a reseller's server; Häfele's live sites exist but refused automated access, and the Wayback Machine could not be reached from this environment [uncertain]
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: 1) Häfele's Minifix clock-face diagram: show a turning connector as angle zones (closing, tightening, re-tightening) so beginners know when to stop turning. 2) Lamello's step timing strip ('Cut ca. 25 s, Drill ca. 15 s, Insert ca. 5 s, Connect ca. 5 s, finished in 50 s') as a quick 'effort' indicator per entry. 3) Lamello's function labels (detachable, invisible, self-clamping, slide-in) map directly onto the flow chart's questions ('do you need to take it apart again?', 'must it be hidden?'). 4) Organise by the hole or groove you can make (biscuit groove, drilled hole, CNC face drilling), which is a good making-method filter. 5) Blum's 'type of motion' table (mechanical vs electrical, opening vs closing) is a neat template for powered vs passive entries. 6) Häfele's choice-of-fitting diagram for lightweight panels (pick the fitting by surface-layer thickness) is a mini decision tree worth copying. 7) Tell the story behind a clever type (IKEA Museum: ten years of prototyping, cut assembly time by half) to make entries memorable
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, many numbers. Häfele Minifix: 15 mm or 12 mm housing hole, drilling distance B = 24 or 34 mm from panel edge, bolt hole 5, 7 or 8 mm, panel thicknesses 12-29 mm, about 5 mm pull in half a turn, hole-size tolerance +1 mm to about -0.5 mm; Maxifix minimum material 19 mm, 3/4 turn; Aerofix 100 pull-out strengths about 300-900 N depending on panel. Lamello Clamex P-14: tolerance ±1 mm, minimum workpiece width 75 mm, minimum material 12-18 mm depending on cut (29 mm for centre wall), tensile strength 1070 N in particle board, 1210 N in MDF, 1870 N in beech, shear 490/600/2940 N, size 64 x 27 x 9.7 mm; clamping force about 80 kg (Clamex P) and about 15 kg (Tenso P); mitres from 22.5 to 180 degrees; 6 mm access hole. Cabineo needs 12 mm minimum panel thickness. Invis Mx2 clamps up to 250 kg per connector. IKEA: wedge dowel needed production tolerances about 2.5 times tighter than before; patent mentions a groove incline of about 2 degrees
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Partly: Lamello's online P-System configurator ('find the right connector for every angle') and LC P-16 configurator give connector choice and milling positions, and Lamello offers CAD/CAM integration for CNC software. No open parametric models or generators
usefulness.file_formats: PDF (Häfele catalogue chapters, IKEA fact sheet, Lamello brochures and operation manuals), CAD downloads from Lamello in DWG, DXF and STEP (connector and machining geometry), video, HTML
usefulness.terminology_value: Medium: good source for trade names and a few generic terms (knock-down/KD fitting, RTA connector, cam connector, connecting bolt, spreading bolt, cross dowel, suspension fitting, positive-locking/form-locking groove, self-clamping, detachable), and Lamello's multilingual site can give German/French equivalents. Weak for neutral names because brand names dominate; Wikipedia's 'knock-down fastener' and 'cam lock' pages are better for the generic name
usefulness.decision_support: Some: Lamello's product finder and P-System configurator (choose by joint angle and application), Häfele's lightweight-panel 'Choice of Fittings' diagram (choose by surface-layer thickness and whether the panel has a frame), Blum's motion-technology comparison table and CLIP top 'hinge range at a glance' by application (standard, wide angle, thick door, blind corner, glass door, angled -45 to 45 degrees). No cross-brand selector
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Overlaps with the existing 'Supplier catalogues as a vocabulary source (McMaster-Carr, MISUMI, igus)' item (latches, hinges, catches), with 'Digital joinery catalogues (Jochen Gros, WikiHouse, IBOIS)' and 'Japanese joinery catalogues' for wood joints, and with DT Online (school wiki) and Wikipedia 'Furniture screw' for generic knock-down fitting names. The IKEA wedge dowel is documented originally in patent US9447804B2 (Inter IKEA Systems; inventors Benny Andersson, Göran Sjöstedt, Anders Eriksson). Similar cam connectors are sold by many other makers (e.g. Hettich, Titus) [uncertain: not opened]
